Verdict

Reviewed 27 Oct 2026 · next 25 Jan 2027

The entry point and the only package most apps import. Supply chain is strong: OIDC trusted publishing, SLSA provenance, no install scripts anywhere in the 183-package tree. The costs are 10 direct dependencies, a 54 MB install, about 135 KB gzip, and 0.x churn of roughly 30 releases per quarter.

Current Reviewed version 0.15.31 Requirement: In-app AI assistant chat interface (React)

Reasoning

  1. Publishing uses OIDC trusted publishing from a protected npm Publish environment. The publish job installs only the Changesets CLI with --ignore-scripts and publishes pre-built tarballs, so no package build runs with publishing credentials.
  2. SLSA provenance for 0.15.31 resolves to assistant-ui/assistant-ui, workflow .github/workflows/npm-publish.yaml, ref refs/heads/main.
  3. The full installed tree is 183 packages: 178 MIT, one ISC, one BSD-3-Clause and one 0BSD, with zero install or postinstall scripts.
  4. React 18 and 19 are both declared and tested by a dedicated react18-weekly workflow; types are bundled.
  5. OSV returns no advisories for any of the suite's latest versions.
  6. Measured about 135 KB gzip for a minimal bundle of AssistantRuntimeProvider + ThreadPrimitive + useLocalRuntime, excluding React.

Caveats

  • ESM-only. require() works on Node 22.12+ (verified on Node 24) but not on older CommonJS runtimes.
  • 0.x versioning: 460 published versions and about 30 releases in the last 90 days. Pin exact versions and upgrade deliberately; ^0.15.x only permits patches.
  • 10 direct dependencies including zod, zustand, radix-ui, assistant-cloud and assistant-stream.
  • One npm maintainer is an automation account (agentbase-bot). Publishing is gated by the GitHub environment, but the account still holds package access.
  • 54 MB install standalone and 63 MB for the full suite; most of that is source and source maps that bundlers discard.

Decision context

Approved

@assistant-ui/react is the primary choice for In-app AI assistant chat interface (React). This package is classified as Adopted.

Adopt @assistant-ui/react as the single direct dependency, plus @assistant-ui/react-markdown only if formatted assistant output is required. @assistant-ui/core, @assistant-ui/tap and @assistant-ui/store arrive transitively and must be allowlisted because they are required peers, not optional extras; @assistant-ui/store was missing from the original four-package list. All five are MIT, provenance-signed, free of install scripts and advisories, and the repository publishes through OIDC trusted publishing with a protected environment. The residual risks are footprint (63 MB full install, about 135 KB gzip) and 0.x churn (roughly 30 releases per quarter), so pin exact versions, import only from @assistant-ui/react, keep rehype-raw disabled, and re-review on the 90-day cadence.
